<strong>Acht von 18 Herkunftsgruppen</st: Eight of 18 origin groups have a district-level breakdown: Turkey, Syria, Kosovo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Iraq, Afghanistan and North Macedonia. They account for around 78 to 83 percent of the state total. The remainder — Pakistan, Morocco, Iran, Lebanon and others — has no district-level figures and is distributed according to migration background.
<strong>Definition der BAMF-Schätzung:</: Definition of the BAMF estimate: People with a migration background from the countries of origin considered, including Alevi adherents. Not all converts and origin groups are covered. The state-level distribution is based on 2019 shares.
<strong>Es gibt daher keine empirisch ab: There is therefore no empirically grounded distribution of the muslim population across districts or municipalities. At the source levels, therefore, selecting a district or municipality does not display a muslim share — instead the figure is marked as missing. The levels “Model by district” and “Model by municipality” distribute the published state total by origin. In the map, profile and export they carry the note “model calculation – not an official religious statistic” and always a range.
<strong>Gemeinden</strong> erhalten kein: Municipalities do not receive their own estimate. The district value is distributed: the Turkish and Bosnian shares follow the settlement pattern measured in the Zensus 2022, the remainder follows the immigration history measured in the Zensus 2022 per municipality. For Syria, Afghanistan, Iraq and Kosovo there is no municipal-level data. The municipal ranges are therefore wider than the district ranges.
<strong>Keine Individualdaten.</strong>: No individual-level data. The project shows exclusively published aggregates or aggregates calculated transparently from them. It contains no residential addresses and no attribution of a religion to individual people.
<strong>T</strong> ist die veröffentlich: T is the published BW range for 2025 (1,133,000–1,197,000). Aₖ,c is the foreign population of citizenship c in district k (Ausländerzentralregister, 31 December 2024). sc is the nationwide muslim share of origin group c (BAMF Forschungsbericht 55, Table 2). rc adds naturalised persons and their descendants born here: persons with a migration background of this origin divided by citizens of the same origin, from the Mikrozensus. MHₖ is the population with a migration background in the district.
<strong>Was das nicht ist:</strong> kein: What this is not: not an official religious statistic, not a survey, not a confidence interval in the statistical sense. The range covers the published state range, the choice of variant and — at municipality level — the choice of distribution key. It does not cover the error in the nationwide origin shares from 2019/2020.
<strong>Zwei Varianten</strong> sind wäh: Two variants are selectable. “Citizenship only” dispenses with rc and distributes the unexplained remainder the same way as the citizenship data itself. The gap between the two variants is part of the uncertainty and is not hidden.
AA-Jahres-PDFs: bearbeitete nationale Vi: Annual PDFs of the Federal Foreign Office: national visas processed. Do not add the total and the sub-categories together.
Absolute Einwohnerzahl, keine Bevölkerun: Absolute population, not population density. The population of municipalities is reported with a different reference date.

Anteil der Bevölkerung ohne deutsche Sta: Share of the population without German citizenship per government region (NUTS 2), added up from the district figures. Naturalised persons and descendants born here hold a German passport and do not appear in these figures.

Share of the population without German citizenship, reference date 31 December 2025. The same measure as the 2024 layer, one year later and updated by the federal government instead of the state. The difference is small: the median across districts is 17.2 percent in both years, and the largest deviation for any district is 0.4 percentage points. Both layers stand side by side so this can be checked rather than simply asserted.
Share of the population without German citizenship. Calculated in-house from concurrent official register data. No indication of religion, country of birth, or parents' origin.
Anteil der Einwohnerinnen und Einwohner: Share of residents without German citizenship, by municipality. Naturalised persons and their children born in Germany count as Germans and are invisible here — in long-established communities that is the majority. A municipality with a low share of foreign nationals can still have a long-established immigrant population. This is measured, not modelled: the only directly recorded figure the atlas can place alongside the model calculation at municipality level.
Anteil der Erwerbspersonen — erwerbstäti: Share of the labour force — in work, or unemployed and looking — among the foreign-born aged 20 to 64. The difference from the unemployment rate is the whole point: someone who neither works nor looks for work appears in no unemployment rate. Two regions with the same unemployment rate can therefore look very different, and the gap to the native-born is shown in the profile.
Anteil der Erwerbstätigen an der Bevölke: Share of employed persons among the population aged 15 and over with a migration background. Sample survey. No unemployment rate, because the source withholds the number of unemployed persons for almost all districts for confidentiality. These figures do not feed into any model calculation in this atlas.
Anteil der Personen ohne Pass des Wohnsi: Share of people without a passport of the country they live in. This is the same definition used on the district and municipal layers of this atlas — unlike country of birth, naturalised citizens are not counted here. What is comparable is the definition, not the number: Eurostat counts only people aged 15 to 64 in private households, and because immigrants are over-represented in those age groups the value is higher than the share across all ages. For the Stuttgart region 25.3 instead of 19.8 per cent.
Anteil der ausländischen Bevölkerung des: Share of the district's foreign population holding Turkish citizenship. Not the number of people of Turkish origin: naturalised persons and their descendants born here hold a German passport and are entirely absent. Nationwide median: 7.5 percent.

Share of the district's foreign population originating from the guest-worker recruitment countries — Turkey, Italy, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Tunisia, former Yugoslavia. The denominator is the district's foreign population, not its total population.

Share of the district's foreign population that has lived in Germany for at least 25 years. This figure, too, counts only people without a German passport — precisely among the long-established, naturalised persons are missing, so the length of stay of origin groups tends to be underestimated. Nationwide median: 17.4 percent.
Anteil der hier geborenen Menschen mit d: Share of people born here with a German passport among the population with a migration background. These are precisely the people missing from the foreign-national statistics — which is why the model calculation needs a correction for naturalised persons and descendants. No indication of religious affiliation.
Anteil der im Ausland Geborenen an der B: Share of foreign-born people among the population aged 15 to 64 in private households. What is counted is the place of birth, not the passport: naturalised citizens are included here and are not included in the foreign-national share of the other layers. Labour Force Survey sample; correspondingly uncertain for small regions.
Anteil der unter 25-Jährigen an der Bevö: Share of people under 25 among the population with a migration background. Hatched: the source withholds too many age groups to form a reliable share. Migration background is a far larger group than the modelled muslim population; this is not that group's age structure.

Share of people under 25 in the population, from the Zensus 2022. Unlike the district layer from the Mikrozensus, this is a full census and available for all municipalities. No indication of religious affiliation and not a variable in the model calculation.
Anteil der unter 25-Jährigen an der ausl: Share of people under 25 among the district's foreign population. Statewide this is 24.6 percent — 24.9 percent for the German population, so practically the same. This is partly an artefact of how the count works: children of immigrants who are naturalised or born German count on the German side and are missing on the foreign side. This is explicitly not a comparison of the age structure of origin groups.
Anteil derer, die 2010 oder später einge: Share of those who arrived in 2010 or later among the foreign-born whose year of arrival is known. A high value means recent immigration, a low one a long-established population — the counterpart to the district layer "resident for 25 years", except that there the passport counts and here the place of birth. From the 2021 census: a full count across all ages, not a sample estimate, but a single snapshot with no update. Cases with no year of arrival are left out of the denominator rather than quietly counted among the long-established; their share is shown in each region's profile. In 15 of the 251 regions — in Czechia, France and Slovakia — it is missing for more than a fifth, in Baden-Württemberg for at most a tenth.
Anteil mit tertiärem Abschluss an den im: Share with a tertiary qualification among the foreign-born aged 25 to 64. This layer separates out one of the four things bundled into the employment rate gap. It also shows what an average conceals: in the Stuttgart region 28.7 per cent of the foreign-born hold a university degree and 35.0 per cent have at most lower secondary education — the group is strongly represented at both ends, not in the middle. Both figures and the gap to the native-born are in each region's profile.
Anteile beziehen sich auf die ausländisc: Shares refer to the district's foreign population, not its total population.

Modellrechnung, keine Messung. Die Gemei: Model calculation, not a measurement. The municipality values distribute the respective district value. The Turkish and Bosnian share follows the settlement pattern measured in the census; the remainder follows the immigration history of each municipality. For Syria, Afghanistan, Iraq and Kosovo there is no municipality-level data of their own. The ranges are correspondingly wide.
Modellrechnung, keine Messung. Die veröf: Model calculation, not a measurement. The published state total is distributed by origin: foreign population by citizenship multiplied by the nationwide muslim share of that origin group. There are no official religious statistics by district.

Näherungswerte über den Anteil muslimisc: Approximate values for the share of Muslims with a migration background from predominantly Islamic countries of origin in the population of each federal state, from Table 3 and Figure 4 of Research Report 55. The colour follows the middle of the published range; the range itself is what is stated. Baden-Württemberg ranks fourth of fourteen at 10.1 to 10.7 per cent, behind Bremen and Hamburg, Hesse and North Rhine-Westphalia — in absolute numbers second, behind North Rhine-Westphalia. Bremen and Hamburg, and Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, are reported only jointly because they were combined when the sample was drawn; the map therefore combines them too, rather than feigning a precision the source does not have.

Punkte sind Einrichtungen, keine Bevölke: Points are institutions, not population figures. Each point sits at the centre of its municipality and does not denote a building: this atlas does not compile an address list. What is documented is the place, and each entry links the source giving the address: the institution's own website, its federation's directory, a city's association register, a state parliament paper, or OpenStreetMap. Places of worship without a federation are mostly sourced from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), which also serves here as a second, independent source. What is included is what is publicly known and publicly documented. A federation affiliation is named only when a source itself states it, together with author and date; otherwise the institution is listed without a federation. No personal data. No number of believers can be derived from institutions.
